label: Review questions
intro: Copied as written from the review questions in the course book. These are not from a past paper.

papers.paper: Review questions from the CSC 421 course book, copied as written (not from a past paper)
papers.source: Operating System CSC 421 for DLC2.docx, the review questions at the end of Units 1 to 10

questions.text:
a. List and explain the different types of O/S?
b. When is an O/S termed a multiprogramming O/S?
c. What is the basic role of an operating system?
d. List and describe the services provided by the O/S.

a. Compare and contrast Internal and External fragmentation.
b. In which allocation scheme are the Bound Register and Relocation Register used?  What are they used for?
c. What is common to all the memory allocation schemes described in this unit?
d. Which memory allocation scheme first allowed multiprogramming? Justify your answer.

a. Differentiate between Segmented memory management and Paged memory management?
b. Define the terms: Page; Segment; Page fault; Internal Fragmentation; External Fragmentation; Swapping; Thrashing
c. Give a vivid example of how shared segments can be use in any software package that you know and use.
d. How can the size of the page frame affect Paged Memory Management.

a. Differentiate between multiprogramming and multiprocessing systems.
b. Assuming you have just been hired to assist HP design a multi-user interactive system applying the concept of multi-processing.  Which configuration would you implement and why would you choose that configuration?

a. When is a process said to be in a critical region?
b. What mechanisms are used to enforce mutual exclusion?  Describe these mechanisms.
c. With suitable examples, describe the problem of Readers and Writers.

a. State the four necessary conditions for deadlock to occur?
b. Differentiate between Deadlock, Starvation and Race condition.
c. When is system said to be in a safe state?
d. List and explain any 4 methods you can use to recover your system from a deadlock situation.

a. What the component of an I/O subsystem and what are their functions?
b. With suitable diagrams, compare and contrast the structure of the hard disk with that of the CD-ROM.
c. System devices can be broadly classified into 3.  List and describe these three.
d. In a bid to reduce the outbreak of malaria on the ground floor of Nando Hall, the hall warden authorized that the rooms on that floor be sprayed by Mr Peace.  There are 30 rooms on that floor and the students are to make requests to Mr. Peace for their room to be sprayed.  At a point in time, Mr. Peace was heading to the beginning of the floor (ie lower room numbers) but stopped in room no. 10 to service a request.  The outstanding requests he has are in the order: 1, 11, 29, 14, 22 room numbers.  It takes Mr Peace, 1 second to move from one room to the next.  Ignoring how long it will take to spray a room, state the sequence of Mr Peace movement along the floor and calculate the total seek time only if he is using:
i. Shortest Seek Time First
ii. FCFS
iii. LOOK

a. What are the two main ways that files are stored on any storage medium?
b. What is fragmentation?
c. In the chained storage, what does a null pointer signify?
d. Why is compaction performed by the operating system?
e. File A is stored using chained storage and File B which is the same size as file A is stored using indexed storage.  Which of the file will occupy more space on the disk?
f. Describe the linked storage with a suitable diagram?
g. Write short notes on any 5 types of File System.

a. Differentiate between Negative feedback loops and positive feedback loops.
b. When doe a system become a bottleneck
c. Write short notes on Turnaround Time, Response Time, System Reaction Time, Throughput.

a. What are the different levels of protecting a system?
b. If a password is made up of 5 characters, how many possible combinations of the characters are there?
c. Can a virus harm your system? How?
